summary.text: A woman with no significant comorbidities presented with a painful swelling behind the right ear for 6 years and facial asymmetry for 1 month. She had previously refused surgery advised by many centers. Examination showed a firm 7 × 4 cm neck swelling with two palpable level II nodes, skin fixity and right grade VI House-Brackmann facial palsy.

Blood tests were unremarkable with no evidence of distant metastasis. MRI showed a 7 × 6 × 4 cm right parotid lesion and necrotic level II and III nodes, and temporal bone HRCT showed facial canal enlargement extending into the tympanic segment. Initial FNAC slides showed basaloid cell clusters, and repeat FNAC findings favored a differential of PLGA, papillary cystic acinic cell carcinoma or AdCC, and a preoperative parotid carcinoma diagnosis (cT4aN2bM0) was made.

After right lateral tarsorrhaphy she underwent right radical parotidectomy with modified radical neck dissection, modified lateral temporal bone resection and pectoralis major myocutaneous flap reconstruction, with retrograde perineural spread into the tympanic segment found intraoperatively. The postoperative period was uneventful. Histopathology showed low- and high-grade areas, facial nerve invasion and 7 of 19 nodes involved (pT4aN3bM0).

Adjuvant radiotherapy was planned but she refused any adjuvant therapy. At 3 months follow-up local recurrence was suspected because of facial swelling and CEMRI was advised, but she refused further treatment. Recurrence and metastasis investigations could not be done, and she died at home 5 months after surgery.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the three images are described in the separate visual submission.
The Fig. 2 caption gives the patient age as 26 years while the case text and Table 2 give 28 years; both ages are kept as review-only source-conflict facts.
The case text gives no dates; times are kept only where the source states them, and event order is limited to stated order wording.
Table 2 rows other than the Current study row describe published literature cases and are not index-patient facts.
The cytology differential is listed as alternatives and none is asserted; the source does not report a frozen section result or the date of the repeat FNAC.
The discussion statement that perineural spread was seen at both levels uses garbled level wording (macroscopic or macroscopic) and is not recorded as a fact.

The discussion sentence that the cited rarity of cervical node metastasis and 40% distant metastasis was in contrast to this case is not recorded as a separate fact because it does not say which attribute contrasts.
